newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia MinFin not to push T-bill yield down- trade.
newsitem.headline: Russia MinFin not to push T-bill yield down- trade.

text.p: Russia's Finance Ministry showed at Wednesday's GKO discount Treasury bills auctions that it was determined not to push already-low yields down any further, dealers said.
*Finance Ministry placed an additional 133-day tranche of series 22084 T-bill at 18.64 pct
*Finance Ministry repaid 8.00 trln rbls in maturing 231-day T-bill issue (series 22057)
"Most bids were placed at an average price and given a relatively high demand the Finance Ministry could have had a lower yield," Natsionalny Rezervny Bank dealer Stanislav Litvinov said.
"But ... the Finance Ministry showed it was not interested in a sharp yield fall," he added.
T-bills yields plummeted a few weeks ago, and analysts said the fall was still making the market unstable, as foreign investors were not yet ready to pay high prices for Russian paper.
Dealers said the current yield resistance level was at 19-20 percent.
A central bank official said at Wednesday's auctions that the Finance Ministry had pumped out excess demand from a market which had already been seeing high demand for several weeks.
Dealers said non-residents, who consider the current yield levels acceptable, accounted for the bulk of that demand.

"Taken into consideration the dynamics of the forward market, the hard currency yield at current rates is 15 percent annual, which means there is still room for a further fall," Probusinessbank dealer Oleg Surkov said.
Litvinov forecast an inflow of fresh funds to the secondary market on Thursday due to the excess of roubles on the interbank market.
"The yields at the auctions were attractive and the money can come," he said. "Most likely we shall see the market nudging up by 0.2-0.3 percentage points on the new paper, and the yields slipping."
